title: Fatigue
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, witnessed apneas, morning headaches, and fatigue. Risk factors: obesity, large neck circumference, male, retrognathia. OSA = repetitive upper airway collapse during sleep → apnea/hypopnea → oxygen desaturation → sympathetic surge → disrupted sleep. STOP-BANG screening questionnaire. Complications: hypertension, atrial fibrillation, pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, metabolic syndrome, motor vehicle accidents. Diagnosis: polysomnography (sleep study) — AHI (apnea-hypopnea index) >5 = OSA. Mild 5-15, moderate 15-30, severe >30. Treatment: CPAP (first-line for moderate-severe). Weight loss (most important lifestyle). Oral appliance for mild-mod. Positional therapy. Surgical (UPPP) if CPAP intolerant.
chief_complaint: Daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, witnessed apneas
